questions.question: Angle subtended by a chord MN on the circumference of a circle is 90 degree. If diameter of the circle is 44 cm. then what will be the length of chord MN?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By the **property of circles**, a chord subtends a 90° angle at the circumference if and only if it is the **diameter** of the circle.

Given **diameter** = 44 cm.

∴ The length of chord **MN** = 44 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 44 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 44 cm

Angle subtended by chord MN at the circumference = 90°

**Formula Used:**

**Angle in a semi-circle:** The angle subtended by the diameter of a circle at any point on its circumference is always 90°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd6df84194e32cff2555710de7e24f88d02603567817efb2ac064f8738acbcf9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let P be any point on the circumference of the circle.

⇒ Given that ∠MPN = 90°.

⇒ According to **Thales’ Theorem**, if an angle subtended by a chord at the circumference is a right angle, then that chord must be the **diameter** of the circle.

⇒ Chord MN = Diameter of the circle

⇒ MN = 44 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 44 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Thales' Theorem

It states that if M, N, and P are points on a circle where the line MN is a diameter, then the angle ∠MPN is a right angle (90°).

Chord and Central Angle

The central angle subtended by the diameter is 180°. Since the angle at the circumference is half the angle at the center, 180° ÷ 2 = 90°.

Longest Chord

The diameter is the longest possible chord in any circle and its length is twice the radius (D = 2 × r).</p

questions.solution:

Ratio of the marked price(MP) of a trouser and a jacket = 1 : 3

Total discount on both of them = 30%

Formula used:

Discount% = (Discount/MP) × 100

Calculation:

Let the MP of trouser and jacket be x and 3x

Discount on trouser = 0.2 × x = 0.2x

Total discount on both = 0.3 × (x + 3x) = 1.2x

⇒ Discount on jacket = 1.2x - 0.2x = x

Discount% on jacket = (x/3x) × 100 = 33.33

questions.question: The radii of two concentric circles are 34 cm and 50 cm. A and D are the points on larger circle and B and C are points on smaller circle. If ABCD is a straight line and BC = 32 cm, then what is the length of AD?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radii of two concentric circles are 34 cm and 50 cm.

ABCD is a straight line and BC = 32 cm.

A and D are the points on larger circle and B and C are points on smaller circle.

**Concept Used:**

Pythagoras theorem

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Perpendicular drawn from the centre to the chord divide the chord into two equal parts.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3710529c3462f5e50abce868e7170d2473683a03a2915e4c60e80d6ce569beb5.png] 

BC = 32 cm

BP = 32/2 = 16 cm

In triangle OBP

Apply Pythagoras Theorem

OB² = BP² + OP²

34² = OP² + 16²

OP² = 1156 - 256

OP² = 900

OP = 30 cm

In triangle OPD

OD² = OP² + PD²

50² = 30² + PD²

PD² = 2500 - 900

PD² = 1600

PD = 40 cm

AD = 2 × PD = 2 × 40 = 80 cm

The length of AD is 80 cm.

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: What amount a man would have received on a principal of Rs. 7,500 after two years at simple interest at the rate of 7 per cent per annum ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 7500

Rate = 7%

Time = 2 years

**Concept Used:**

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

**Calculation:**

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Simple Interest = (7500 × 7 × 2)/100

Simple Interest = Rs. 1050

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

Amount = 7500 + 1050

Amount = Rs. 8550

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: In Δ XYZ, points P, Q and R are points on the sides XY, YZ and XZ respectively ∠YXZ = 50 degree, XR = PR, ZR = QR and ∠RQZ = 80 degree. What is the value of ∠PRQ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠YXZ = 50 degree

XR = PR, ZR = QR 

∠RQZ = 80 degree

**Concept Used:**

If two sides of the triangle are equal then the triangle is isosceles triangle. The two angles opposite to the equal sides are congruent to each other.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9842f1848f8de2e24f367a79b1134b12a25b8b379d1a4f6ab73a3a4e1bbf12d9.png] 

In Δ XPR,

∠PXR = 50° 

PR = XR

∴ Triangle is isosceles

∠XPR = ∠PXR = 50° 

∠XRP = 180° - 50° - 50° 

∠XRP = 80°

Similarly,

∠RQZ = ∠RZQ = 80° 

∠QRZ = 180° - 80° - 80° 

∠QRZ = 20° 

Now,

∠PRQ = 180° - 20° - 80° = 80° 

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Distance of a chord JK from the centre is 7 cm. If diameter of this circle is 50 cm, then what will be length of this chord?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a circle, the **radius**, **distance from center**, and **half-chord length** form a **right-angled triangle**.

Radius (r) = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm. Distance (d) = 7 cm.

Using the **Pythagorean triplet** (7, 24, 25):

Half-chord length = 24 cm.

Length of chord **JK** = 2 × 24 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 50 cm

Distance of chord **JK** from centre (**O**) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2

In ▵**OMJ** (Right-angled), **OJ² = OM² + MJ²** (Pythagoras Theorem)

Chord length **JK** = 2 × **MJ** (Perpendicular from center bisects the chord)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86d7329b3da31f25dc3ac04003c489f57acd3c903ee6907c5ae688bbee67bd56.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm

⇒ In right ▵**OMJ**, **OJ** = 25 cm and **OM** = 7 cm

⇒ **MJ²** = **OJ²** − **OM²**

⇒ **MJ²** = 25² − 7²

⇒ **MJ²** = 625 − 49 = 576

⇒ **MJ** = √576 = 24 cm

⇒ Total length of chord **JK** = 2 × **MJ**

⇒ **JK** = 2 × 24 = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Property

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers that satisfy a² + b² = c², such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17), are extremely useful for quick circle calculations.

Chord Distance Relation

Chords that are equidistant from the center of a circle are equal in length, and longer chords are closer to the center.</p

questions.question: How many numbers are there between 501 and 701 which are divisible by 10 but are not divisible by 3?

 A number is divisible by 10 if its last digit is 0.

questions.question: If the diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm, then what is the perimeter of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The side of a rhombus is the hypotenuse of a right triangle formed by half of its diagonals.

Side = √((d₁ ÷ 2)² + (d₂ ÷ 2)²)

⇒ Side = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 cm

Perimeter = 4 × Side = 4 × 13 = 52 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 52 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first diagonal (AC) = 24 cm

Length of second diagonal (BD) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90°).

By Pythagoras theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Perimeter of a rhombus = 4 × side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/906a57d5508fcceb8742c10902feb956681acd374d795c10645d487ad944784f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Half of diagonal AC (OA) = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ Half of diagonal BD (OB) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm

⇒ In right-angled ΔAOB, the intersection at center O forms a 90° angle.

⇒ Applying Pythagoras theorem in ΔAOB:

⇒ AB² = OA² + OB²

⇒ a² = 12² + 5²

⇒ a² = 144 + 25

⇒ a² = 169

⇒ a = √169 = 13 cm

⇒ The perimeter of the rhombus = 4 × a

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 13 = 52 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 52 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Formula for Perimeter

The perimeter of a rhombus can be calculated directly from its diagonals using the formula: P = 2 × √(d₁² + d₂²).

Area of Rhombus

The area of a rhombus is half the product of the lengths of its diagonals: Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂.

Properties of Rhombus

All four sides of a rhombus are equal in length, and opposite sides are parallel. Its diagonals bisect interior angles and are perpendicular bisectors of each other.
</p

questions.question: If a² + b² + c² = 62 and a + b + c = 12, then what is the value of 4ab + 4bc + 4ca?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

a2 + b2 + c2 = 62

a + b + c = 12

**Formula used:**

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

**Calculation:**

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

12² = 62 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

144 = 62 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

82 = 2(ab + bc + ca)

41 = ab + bc + ca

The value we want to find is 4 times this, so:

4ab + 4bc + 4ca = 4 × 41 = 164

**So, 4ab + 4bc + 4ca = 164.**

questions.question: The average of 15 numbers is 53. A number is removed and the average of 14 numbers now becomes 55. Which number was removed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of 15 numbers is 53.

The average of 14 numbers is 55.

**Calculation:**

Let's denote:

N = the number that was removed.

The sum of the initial 15 numbers can be calculated as 15 × Average = 15 × 53 = 795.

The sum of the 14 remaining numbers can be calculated as 14 × Average = 14 × 55 = 770.

The number removed is the difference between these two sums:

N = 795 - 770 = 25

**So, the number that was removed is 25.**

4 men and 7 women can do a work in 8 days. 7 men and 4 women can do the same work in 5 days. Find the number of days in which 8 women can finish the work.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equating total work: (4M + 7W) × 8 = (7M + 4W) × 5

⇒ 32M + 56W = 35M + 20W ⇒ 3M = 36W ⇒ M = 12W

Total Work = (4 × 12W + 7W) × 8 = 440W units

Time for 8 women = 440W ÷ 8W = 55 days

**∴ The correct answer is 55 Days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

4 men and 7 women complete the work in 8 days.

7 men and 4 women complete the work in 5 days.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 4M + 7W
 8
 40
 5
 
 

 7M + 4W
 5
 8
 
 

**Calculations:**

Let the efficiency of 1 man be M and 1 woman be W.

⇒ 4M + 7W = 5 . . . . (1)

⇒ 7M + 4W = 8 . . . . (2)

Multiplying equation (1) by 7 and equation (2) by 4:

⇒ 28M + 49W = 35

⇒ 28M + 16W = 32

Subtracting the two equations:

⇒ 33W = 3

⇒ W = 1/11

Efficiency of 8 women = 8 × (1/11) = 8/11

Time taken by 8 women = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of 8 women

⇒ Time taken = 40 ÷ (8/11)

⇒ Time taken = (40 × 11) ÷ 8 = 55 days

**∴ The correct answer is 55 Days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total Work is assumed as the LCM of the days taken by different groups to simplify calculation of individual efficiencies, keeping fractions to a minimum until the final steps.

MDH Formula

(M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M is number of workers, D is days, H is hours per day, and W is the total work done.

Pipes & Cisterns Analogy

Follows the exact same efficiency principles as Time & Work, where an inlet pipe represents positive work (filling) and an outlet pipe represents negative work (emptying).
</p

questions.question: Price of 15 chairs is 20 percent more than the price of 8 tables, If price of 2 tables is Rs. 2400, then what is the price of 15 chairs?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Price of 15 chairs is 20% more than the price of 8 tables.

Price of 2 tables is Rs. 2400.

**Calculation:**

Let's denote:

P_C = Price of 15 chairs.

P_T = Price of 8 tables.

We know from the given conditions:

P_C = 1.2 × P_T

P_T = 4 × Price of 2 tables (since 2 × 4 = 8)

Substitute the given value of the price of 2 tables into the second equation:

P_T = 4 × 2400 = Rs. 9600

Substitute this into the first equation to get the price of 15 chairs:

P_C = 1.2 × 9600 = Rs. 11,520

**So, the price of 15 chairs is Rs. 11,520.**

questions.question: What is the value of (1+tan A)/(cosec A)+(1+cot A)/(sec A)?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

** (1+tan A)/(cosec A)+(1+cot A)/(sec A)**

⇒ ** (1+frac{sin A)/(cos A)}{(1)/(sin A)}+ (1+frac{cos A)/(sin A)}{(1)/(cos A)}**

⇒ ** (frac{cos A+sin A)/(cos A)}{(1)/(sin A)}+ (frac{sin A +cos A)/(sin A)}{(1)/(cos A)}**

⇒ (sin A(cos A+sin A))/(cos A)+{(cos A(sin A +cos A))/(sin A)}

⇒ (cos A+sin A)[(sin A)/(cos A)+{(cos A)/(sin A)}]

⇒ (cos A+sin A)[(sin² A + cos ²)/(sin Acos A)]

⇒ [((cos A+sin A))/(sin Acos A)]

⇒ sec A + cosec A

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**
